plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 based on prior iteration evidence. Iteration_15 achieved best_target_score=0.9094 with 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 stack, outperforming iteration_19's 24-layer design (0.6859). Feedback directives require: (1) 50% reduction in per-layer perturbation bounds, (2) cooldown schedule locking outer layers after 2 iterations, (3) adaptive quarter-wave seeding from round 3 refractive index observations. Three complementary routes proposed: Route 1 tightens bounds around iteration_15's best candidate with outer-layer freezing; Route 2 uses adaptive multi-wavelength quarter-wave initialization; Route 3 tests 18-layer configuration for simplicity-performance tradeoff. All routes preserve the 20-layer alternating topology principle that proved effective, with concrete executable modifications.

routes.title: 20-Layer Dual-Band Filter with Reduced Perturbation and Outer-Layer Locking
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing thickness perturbation bounds by 50% around iteration_15's best candidate (65/114/77/93/69/108/70/96/66/67/42/83/51/89/60/67/46/70/50/70 nm) while freezing outer 4 layers after 2 optimization iterations will improve convergence stability and maintain dual-band performance without degrading the 0.909 target score baseline.
routes.design_principle: Local exploitation with constrained search space: tight bounds prevent escape from proven high-performing region; outer-layer locking reduces effective dimensionality and prevents edge-effect instability during late-stage optimization.
routes.proposed_topology: 20 finite layers: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2 on fused silica substrate, air superstrate

Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band

Outer layers frozen to reduce deposition sequence sensitivity

routes.execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air superstrate. Initialize thicknesses at [65, 114, 77, 93, 69, 108, 70, 96, 66, 67, 42, 83, 51, 89, 60, 67, 46, 70, 50, 70] nm (iteration_15 best candidate). Apply optimization bounds of ±15 nm (50% reduction from iteration_15's ±30 nm). Implement cooldown schedule: after 2 optimization iterations, lock layers 1-2 and 19-20 (outermost 4 layers) at their current values. Optimize remaining 16 layers using gradient_thickness optimizer. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light, coherent assumption across all layers. Spectrum: 400-1600 nm with 2001 points. Objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm, maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm. Robustness: relative uniform thickness uncertainty ±20% across 400-1600 nm. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Implements feedback directive: 50% perturbation reduction (±30nm to ±15nm) and outer-layer locking after 2 iterations. Builds on iteration_15's best_target_score=0.9094 while adding convergence stability mechanisms.

routes.title: 20-Layer Adaptive Quarter-Wave Seeding from Effective Index Observations
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing thicknesses using adaptive quarter-wave calculations based on weighted average refractive indices observed in iteration_11 (round 3) will provide physically-motivated starting points that respect local dispersion properties, leading to faster convergence and potentially higher target scores than arbitrary or single-wavelength quarter-wave initialization.
routes.design_principle: Multi-wavelength quarter-wave matching: calculate effective optical thickness using dispersion-weighted average index across both target bands (400-700 nm and 1530-1565 nm), then optimize from this physically-informed baseline rather than single reference wavelength.
routes.proposed_topology: 20 finite layers: HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2|HfO2|SiO2 on fused silica substrate, air superstrate

routes.execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air superstrate. Calculate initial thicknesses using adaptive quarter-wave formula: d = lambda_eff / (4 * n_eff), where lambda_eff is weighted average of 550 nm (visible center) and 1550 nm (IR center), and n_eff is dispersion-weighted average refractive index from iteration_11 round 3 observations. Apply optimization bounds of ±30 nm around initialized values. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with no layer locking. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light, coherent assumption across all layers. Spectrum: 400-1600 nm with 2001 points. Objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm, maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm. Robustness: relative uniform thickness uncertainty ±20% across 400-1600 nm. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Implements feedback directive: adaptive quarter-wave seeding from round 3 refractive index observations. Tests whether dispersion-aware initialization outperforms iteration_15's fixed 550 nm quarter-wave approach.

routes.title: 18-Layer Dual-Band Filter for Simplicity-Performance Tradeoff
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 20 to 18 while maintaining alternating HfO2/SiO2 topology will achieve comparable dual-band performance (target_score within 10% of iteration_15's 0.9094) while improving manufacturing simplicity and reducing deposition time, demonstrating that 20 layers may exceed minimum requirements for this spectral separation task.
routes.design_principle: Layer count minimization: test whether 18 layers (9 HfO2/SiO2 pairs) can achieve acceptable dual-band performance, trading marginal performance loss for manufacturing simplicity and cost reduction.

research_influence: Evidence ID s2-chunk:CorpusId:92993850:s2chunk:92993850:1765:3736:69b2ad685bc8c493 confirms telecom C-band (1550 nm) importance for satellite quantum communication, motivating the dual-band spectral separation objective but does not prescribe specific layer topology or thickness distribution.

Prior iteration evidence (iteration_15 best_target_score=0.9094) directly influenced route designs: all three routes preserve the 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 topology that proved most effective, with route_3 testing whether 18 layers can achieve comparable performance.
Feedback directives from iteration_19 reflection directly shaped route_1 (50% perturbation reduction, outer-layer locking) and route_2 (adaptive quarter-wave seeding from round 3 observations).
unresolved_decisions: Whether outer-layer locking after 2 iterations improves or degrades final optimization quality - requires empirical testing in route_1
Whether adaptive quarter-wave seeding from dispersion-weighted indices outperforms single-wavelength (550 nm) initialization - requires comparison in route_2
Whether 18 layers can achieve acceptable dual-band performance or 20 layers are necessary - requires route_3 results
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
